title: Capture UTMs on landing + propagate into analytics events (attribution stitching)
author: Logan Wright
description: Context: Growth is launching lifecycle onboarding email + retargeting experiments and needs consistent campaign attribution across (a) marketing landing pages and (b) in-product activation funnel events. Today we only log referrer at the edge and lose UTMs once the user signs in / navigates into Console. This PR adds a small, privacy-reviewed UTM capture layer in Console + API that persists a short-lived attribution context and attaches it to eligible analytics events as event properties. Scope: (1) client-side capture of utm_* + gclid on first session (querystring) and storage in a 7-day TTL cookie + localStorage fallback; (2) server-side parsing from request query/cookies and propagation into the server event emitter for key funnel events; (3) schema updates + allowlist enforcement (length caps, character allowlist) so we don’t accidentally ship PII through campaign fields; (4) QA hooks + debug logging behind a dev flag to validate end-to-end stitching. This is intentionally minimal: no new user tables, no cross-domain tracking, and no backfilling. It only enriches events that already exist. Links: ENG-2844. Notes: the UTM fields are added as optional event props, and we keep them out of error logs and traces. The console banner/checklist PRs can now rely on these fields for experiment reporting joins (see attribution conventions doc). Privacy review checklist included below with explicit confirmation from Marketing Ops on naming conventions.

conversation: Tyler Benson: Can we make sure we capture UTMs on the very first landing even if the user immediately signs in via GitHub SSO? We’ve seen query params get lost on the /auth redirect. Logan Wright (author): Added `preserveUtmsOnAuthRedirect` helper; we persist the attribution context before kicking off auth and also attempt to rehydrate from the callback URL if present. For strict cases, the cookie is set pre-redirect so we keep it. Paula Mendes: Please confirm we’re not attaching UTMs to every event. We only want these on lifecycle/activation events (and maybe page_view) so we don’t balloon payload sizes. Logan Wright: Updated allowlist in `emit.ts` so we attach attribution only to: page_view, signup_started, api_key_created, first_request_success, first_streaming_success, dashboard_viewed, billing_added (plus any experiment_exposure events). Everything else remains unchanged. Nadia Rahman: Request: length cap + character filtering. I’m worried about vendors stuffing emails into utm_campaign. Logan Wright: Added sanitize() with: (a) max length 128 per field, (b) printable ASCII + a small set of separators, (c) drop values containing '@' to reduce accidental PII, (d) record `utm_dropped_reason` in debug mode only (not shipped in analytics). Sean Gallagher: Any chance this adds overhead to the critical request path? Middleware on every request makes me nervous. Logan Wright: Middleware is only registered on routes that emit analytics server-side (auth callback + activation endpoints) and is O(1) parsing of cookie header. Also guarded by size caps; if cookie > 1KB we ignore it. Added a small perf note + unit test for large cookie behavior. Jada Williams: For experiment analysis, can we include a stable attribution_id so we can stitch across client/server events without relying on utm_campaign matching? Logan Wright: Added `attribution_id` UUID generated on first capture (stored alongside UTMs). It’s included as an event prop where attribution is attached. Not used for user tracking outside of analytics joins; TTL matches UTM TTL (7 days). Tyler Benson: Please align naming to our UTM conventions exactly (utm_source/medium/campaign/content/term) and include gclid for Google. Logan Wright: Confirmed; keys are exactly those. Also added `msclkid`? Tyler said not needed for this sprint, so omitted. Final pass: updated docs/internal/attribution/utm-debugging.md with steps and screenshots callouts. Approvals: Tyler Benson approved after naming confirmation. Paula Mendes approved after scoping to specific events. Nadia Rahman approved after sanitization changes.
release_notes: Internal: Adds UTM + gclid capture (7-day TTL) and attaches attribution context to activation funnel analytics events for lifecycle experiment measurement.
qa_steps: 1) Open an incognito window and visit https://console.redwoodinference.com/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=llm-benchmarks&utm_content=card-a&utm_term=serverless&gclid=test123
2) Open DevTools > Application > Cookies and confirm `rw_attribution` cookie exists (expires ~7 days). Also confirm localStorage fallback key `rw_attribution_v1` is set.
3) Complete signup/login flow (SSO if applicable) and ensure the cookie persists across redirect.
4) Trigger an analytics event (e.g., view dashboard, create API key, make first request) and verify the event payload includes utm_* + gclid + attribution_id in the network request to analytics.
5) Confirm non-allowlisted events (e.g., console_error, background_poll) do NOT include utm fields.
6) Validate sanitization: set utm_campaign=email-test@example.com and confirm utm_campaign is dropped (absent in payload).
7) Regression: confirm no PII appears in server logs/traces; grep for 'utm_' in server logs after running steps 1-4 (should be none).
privacy_review_checklist: Data minimization: Only captures standard utm_* and gclid; no custom arbitrary query params.
TTL: 7 days; no long-term storage in user profile DB.
Scope: Attached only to a small allowlist of lifecycle/activation events + page_view and experiment_exposure.
PII controls: Drops values containing '@'; caps length to 128; restricts characters; ignores oversized cookie values.
User choice: Respects existing marketing opt-out signals for outbound messaging; attribution capture is first-party and used for product analytics only (no email sending logic here).
Access controls: Attribution fields follow existing analytics pipeline access policies; no new sinks introduced.
Security: Cookie is SameSite=Lax; Secure; path=/; no cross-domain sharing; no third-party pixels added.
Logging: No UTMs written to application logs or tracing spans; debug mode is local/dev only.
Docs: Added internal debugging guide + notes on how to request changes to allowlist/schema.
